questions.prompt: A police officer signals you to stop while your traffic light is green. What should you do?

options.text: Stop as directed by the officer.
options.explanation: A police officer's directions take precedence over traffic signals, signs and general rules.
The officer's instruction has higher priority than the light.

options.text: Stop only if there is a stop sign
options.explanation: The police instruction is sufficient.

options.text: Continue if the road looks clear
options.explanation: A clear road does not cancel the instruction.

questions.correct_answer: Stop as directed by the officer.
questions.question_explanation: A police officer's directions take precedence over traffic signals, signs and general rules.

KörkortGo · M03-L02
M03-L02
Combine the instructions
Your goal: Interpret signs, panels, markings and signals together, including authorised
directions.
Requirements. Follow the traffic instructions that apply to you. Where an instruction differs from
a general traffic rule, the instruction governs. A steady traffic-light indication takes precedence
over a yield or stop sign; a police officer's direction takes precedence over the rules and ordinary
traffic instructions. This is not a rule that a green signal cancels every other restriction.
Authorised guards also give traffic directions that must be followed. Traffic Regulation, chapter 2
§§2–4
Authorised directions
Separate examples. A static picture does not show the complete movement; read the description and the official
instruction.
P1 · Police stop instruction — front and rear
Stopp
Traffic approaching the officer from the front or rear must
stop; traffic approaching from the sides may proceed. The
officer's continuing orientation matters even after the arm
movement. Officer faces the viewer with one arm extended
sideways.
Transportstyrelsen · official description

questions.prompt: You approach a give-way sign with a clear view and no conflicting traffic. What is required?

options.text: Slow down, check carefully and stop only if necessary.
options.explanation: Giving way requires you to avoid obstructing intersecting traffic; a complete stop is not automatic.
A give-way sign does not impose a fixed stop.

options.text: Maintain speed because the road is empty
options.explanation: You must clearly demonstrate readiness to yield.

options.text: Give way only to vehicles from the right
options.explanation: The duty covers traffic from both directions.

questions.correct_answer: Slow down, check carefully and stop only if necessary.
questions.question_explanation: Giving way requires you to avoid obstructing intersecting traffic; a complete stop is not automatic.

These are learning questions, not substitutes for the individual sign descriptions. A warning of
children, for example, does not assign a new numerical speed by itself; your speed must still
allow safe control and a response to foreseeable hazards. A posted maximum speed is a ceiling,
not a demand to maintain that speed. Road Signs Regulation, chapter 2 · Traffic Regulation,
chapter 3 §§14–15
Requirements. B1 means yield to vehicles on the crossing road or route. Make that intention
clear early and proceed only without danger or obstruction. B2 requires a stop before entering
the crossing road or track area. Stop at the stop line; without one, stop immediately before the
signal or before entering the crossing road or track area, as applicable. A rolling pause does not
meet a stop duty. Road Signs Regulation, B1–B2 · Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§5 and 19

Different duties apply when entering a road from premises, a car park, fuel station, similar
roadside area, path or similar exit, or from terrain, a pedestrian street, walking-speed area or
cycle street. After crossing a footway or cycle path to enter a road, the exit provision also
matters. Do not decide solely from a kerb's appearance; identify the actual layout. Joining a
priority road without an acceleration lane generally requires yielding, subject to the provision for
joining without changing lane. Roundabout entry has its own duty. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3
§§21–23
To yield, show your intention by reducing speed or stopping in good time. Only continue when
the other road user's position, distance and speed allow movement without danger or
obstruction. A stop duty requires a complete stop even if the road appears empty. Traffic
Regulation, chapter 3 §§5 and 19

options.explanation: The priority-to-the-right rule applies when no sign, signal or other priority rule replaces it.
This reverses the rule.
Vehicle size does not establish priority.

options.text: Nobody if your road is wider
options.explanation: Road width alone does not change the rule.

questions.question_explanation: The priority-to-the-right rule applies when no sign, signal or other priority rule replaces it.

KörkortGo · M04-L01
M04-L01
Decide who goes first
Your goal: Explain junction decisions using priority instructions and right-hand priority,
and recognise special situations.
Requirements. Where two vehicle paths cross, the general rule is to yield to a vehicle
approaching from your right, except where another applicable rule or instruction determines the
relationship. Road width, familiarity or the fact that you are travelling straight does not by itself
establish priority. Right-hand priority can apply at a three-way junction or within a parking area.
Right-hand priority · Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §18
Priority and junction instructions
Independent examples: A29 variants show different branch layouts. Read thick and thin roads on each T15 panel; do
not assume an approach orientation.
A28 · Junction with right-hand priority
Varning för vägkorsning
The junction ahead is governed by the right-hand priority rule.
Do not assume the broader road has priority. Black cross
inside a warning triangle.
Transportstyrelsen · official description

options.text: The narrower road always gives way
options.explanation: Width alone is not a priority rule.

options.text: You go first if travelling straight
options.explanation: Going straight does not override priority to the right.
Speed never creates priority.

Right turn beside a cyclist: the cycling route and receiving road remain open. Check the cyclist’s movement before

Ordinary vehicle signals
Red, red/amber, green and amber appear in that order. Flashing amber is a separate condition, not the next stage of

Röd

KörkortGo · M04-L02
M04-L02
Turn with a complete picture
Your goal: Plan observation, signalling, position and margins for turns and lane changes.
Requirements. Before a turn, check that it will not obstruct oncoming traffic or traffic on the
road you are entering. Pay attention to people travelling in the same direction, including those
behind you. Position early: normally the right-hand lane for a right turn and the left-hand lane
for a left turn where multiple approach lanes exist, subject to applicable signs, markings and
space provisions. On a two-way road, a left turn is normally prepared near the road centre; on a
one-way carriageway, near the left edge. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§24–29

questions.prompt: Your signal turns green, but the road beyond the junction is blocked. What should you do?

options.text: Wait before entering until you can clear the junction.
options.explanation: You must avoid becoming stationary where you obstruct crossing traffic.

options.text: Enter because the signal is green
options.explanation: Green does not authorise blocking the junction.

options.text: Stop in the middle to reserve your place
options.explanation: That obstructs other traffic.

options.text: Drive onto the pedestrian crossing and wait
options.explanation: The crossing must also be kept clear.

questions.correct_answer: Wait before entering until you can clear the junction.
questions.question_explanation: You must avoid becoming stationary where you obstruct crossing traffic.

KörkortGo · M03-L02 · Worked decision
Apply the learning
A green signal and a queue beyond the junction. Opposing traffic is separated and the stop line is before the
crossing road. The scene is illustrative, not to scale.
Worked decision. Your signal is green, but a queue fills the space beyond the junction. Wait
where you will not obstruct crossing traffic rather than entering a space you cannot clear. Traffic
Regulation, chapter 3 §20
Knowledge check. Does amber mean accelerate to beat red?
Remember: Read the whole instruction and the space beyond it.

options.text: Slow down and let the bus leave.
options.explanation: At a speed limit of 50 km/h or lower, drivers in the affected lane must allow a signalling bus out.
That frustrates the bus rule.

options.text: The bus always has to wait
options.explanation: The 50 km/h rule applies here.
That introduces a new danger.

questions.correct_answer: Slow down and let the bus leave.
questions.question_explanation: At a speed limit of 50 km/h or lower, drivers in the affected lane must allow a signalling bus out.

KörkortGo · M05-L01 · Continued
Continue the learning
T10 · People with impaired hearing
Nedsatt hörsel
People with impaired hearing commonly use the area. Do not
assume a horn will be heard. Three black dots inside a black
circle on yellow.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
Horses and riders also belong in your traffic assessment. Vehicle rules apply to riding and leading
horses in relevant respects; they are not simply pedestrians because they travel slowly. Give
them an unhurried, spacious interaction, and avoid unnecessary noise. This is a cautious
application of the general duty of care, not a fixed passing-distance rule. Transportstyrelsen:
horses in traffic
Horses and riders
This warning supports early observation. It does not specify a fixed passing distance.
A18 · Horse riders ahead
Varning för ridande
Riders often cross or use this stretch of road. Prepare for an
unhurried, spacious encounter. Horse and rider inside a
warning triangle.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
Bus rule. Where the maximum permitted speed is 50 km/h or lower, a driver approaching a bus
whose driver signals to leave a bus stop must slow and give it the opportunity to leave, stopping
if needed. The bus driver must also take particular care. If passing on the right of a bus or tram
stopped at a stop without a refuge, stop to allow boarding or alighting passengers free passage.
Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§45 and 58

questions.prompt: The speed limit is 70 km/h and a bus signals to leave its stop. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The bus must give way, but you should still be ready to cooperate.
options.explanation: The special obligation to let a bus out applies at limits of 50 km/h or lower.

options.text: The bus always has unconditional priority
options.explanation: The limit is above the bus-rule threshold.

options.text: You should block the bus deliberately
options.explanation: All drivers still owe care and consideration.

options.text: The bus may pull out without looking
options.explanation: Its driver must avoid danger.

questions.correct_answer: The bus must give way, but you should still be ready to cooperate.
questions.question_explanation: The special obligation to let a bus out applies at limits of 50 km/h or lower.
questions.rationale: The 50 km/h threshold is taught, but the bus yielding duty above it is not explained.

Amber is not an invitation to speed up.

options.text: Continue whenever the junction is empty
options.explanation: An empty junction does not remove the stop requirement.
That can make the stop unsafe or too late.

questions.question_explanation: Amber means stop unless you are so close that stopping safely is no longer possible.

KörkortGo · M04-L04 · Continued
Continue the learning
Learning approach. Read the layout before reaching the yield point. Reduce speed enough to
judge circulating traffic and the available space. Observe crossings on the approach as separate
conflicts. Inside, hold your intended path and continue checking nearby vehicles. A large vehicle
may need more room than its apparent lane width suggests. Roundabout guide
Plan the exit early. Moving from an inner lane across an outer lane is a lane change, even though
you call the whole movement “leaving the roundabout.” Do not assume a vehicle beside you will
leave at the same exit. If the exit cannot be taken safely, continue as the layout allows and
re-plan. On leaving, check the crossing area again; the duties in M04-L03 still apply. Roundabout
guide · Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§60–62

Approach: B1 and D3 identify the entry instructions.
The teal car approaches the yield point while the
yellow car circulates anticlockwise.
Circulation: two lanes surround the island. The teal car
in the inner lane and yellow car in the outer lane need
separate space; the inner lane confers no exit priority.
Worked decision. Your desired exit is approaching, but a car is alongside in the outer lane. You
do not cut across it. You preserve a safe path and choose another opportunity consistent with
the lane markings. Recovering the route is secondary to avoiding a conflict.

KörkortGo · M06-L02
M06-L02
Is passing worth the risk?
Your goal: Compare waiting with overtaking using visibility, speed difference, space and a
safe completion path.
Requirements. Overtake only without danger and with sufficient clear road. Do not start when a
following driver has begun overtaking, or pass on the left when the vehicle ahead signals an
intended leftward movement. Leave safe lateral clearance and a safe return opportunity. When
being overtaken, do not increase speed or otherwise make the pass harder. Traffic Regulation,
chapter 3 §§31–38
The normal passing side is left. Exceptions include a vehicle turning or clearly preparing to turn
left, and the specified rules for marked same-direction lanes on roads limited to 70 km/h or less.
Passing in queues or destination lanes has separate provisions; it does not remove the need to
protect people at crossings. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§7, 31 and 41–42
Restrictions to recognise. Overtaking is generally prohibited immediately before or in a road
junction, with specified exceptions for right-side overtaking, police/signal control, or an
established yielding/stopping duty on the crossing road. Similar restrictions apply at level
crossings, with exceptions for barriers or road-junction-type traffic signals. At an obscured bend
or crest, do not use an opposing lane to overtake; the detailed provision contains limited
exceptions. Section 39 also contains an exception for passing two-wheeled vehicles without
sidecars. That exception does not override the danger prohibition, continuous-line restrictions
or the uncontrolled-crossing prohibition. None of these exceptions proves a manoeuvre safe.
Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §39
Do not overtake immediately before or on an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing, uncontrolled
cycle passage or cycle crossing. Where parallel-lane passing is legally not classified as
overtaking, the special crossing rule still requires a speed allowing an immediate stop for a
person on the crossing or passage. Obey signs and continuous-line restrictions as well. Traffic
Regulation, chapter 3 §§11, 40–41

KörkortGo · M03-L04
M03-L04
Leave room to respond
Your goal: Explain how observation, speed, reaction, braking, grip and following space
affect your options.
Requirements. Choose a speed that preserves control and lets you stop within the road you can
see and before a foreseeable obstruction. Your distance from the vehicle ahead must allow for it
slowing or stopping. Weather, visibility, road condition, vehicle condition and loading all matter.
Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§2 and 14–16
For an ordinary car, the general speed limits are 50 km/h within a built-up area and 70 km/h
outside it, unless another applicable limit has been prescribed. The motorway default is 110
km/h; 120 km/h can be prescribed. Local and road-specific limits often differ, and a lower
vehicle-combination limit still applies. Read the current signs and conditions rather than
selecting a speed from the road’s appearance. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §17, chapter 4 §20
and chapter 9 §1
Limits and road regimes
Numeric maximum-speed examples are independent. Start and end types are labelled individually; unequal values
do not form a sequence.
C31 · Maximum speed
Hastighetsbegränsning
Do not exceed the displayed speed in km/h. A junction alone
does not necessarily end the limit, and conditions may require
a lower speed. Red-bordered yellow circle displaying 30:
maximum 30 km/h.
Transportstyrelsen · official description

KörkortGo · M06-L02 · Illustration
Assess the whole passing path
Learning approach. Before moving, identify the full pass and return path, not merely the first
gap. If completing it depends on another driver braking or on exceeding the limit, decline it.
Small apparent time savings are not a reason to consume every margin. Trafikverket: speed and
journey time
Following a slower vehicle towards a hidden bend. The visible straight does not establish a complete pass and
return path. The depicted spacing is illustrative, not a recommended following distance.
Worked decision. A vehicle ahead travels slightly slower than you want. An approaching bend
hides the final part of the pass. You stay behind at a useful distance. The first few clear metres do
not establish a complete overtaking opportunity.

KörkortGo · M05-L02 · Continued
Continue the learning
Motor vehicles may use a pedestrian street only to cross it, apart from the specified necessary
journeys: goods to or from shops or equivalent premises; goods or residents to or from
addresses there; guests to or from hotels or equivalent premises; and sick people or people with
mobility impairments to or from an address. A convenient shortcut does not qualify. Check
additional signs and local restrictions. Traffic Regulation, chapter 8 §1
On a cycle street (cykelgata), the maximum is 30 km/h, and motor vehicles must adapt speed to
bicycle traffic. Vehicles entering from another road yield to vehicles already on it. Parking is
restricted to specially provided places. When leaving a cycle street for another road, the exit
yielding rule applies. Special streets · Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §21 and chapter 8 §1a

KörkortGo · M02-L04
M02-L04
Move with control
Your goal: Plan observation and control for starting, stopping, reversing, hill starts and
turning, and explain why supervised practice is needed.
Requirements. Before moving away from the edge, changing position or lane, you must ensure
the movement can be made without danger or unnecessary obstruction. Turning around and
reversing must be possible without danger or obstruction to other road users. Signal your
intention where required, but a signal does not give you priority. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3
§§43, 46 and 65–66
Learning approach. Break a manoeuvre into preparation, observation, controlled movement
and reassessment. Choose a place with enough room; check around the vehicle and along the
intended path; move only while the space remains safe. Stop and reassess when the view
changes. Looking once before starting is not continuous observation.
A hill start is a control task: prevent unintended movement while coordinating the actual
vehicle's transmission, brakes and accelerator. Do not copy pedal sequences between cars
without instruction. Reversing, parking and turning also need practical feedback about vehicle
dimensions and the path followed by its corners. The official practical test may examine these
skills, including effective braking. Practise braking exercises only in suitable, supervised
conditions—not as an experiment in ordinary traffic. Trafikverket: manoeuvring and braking
The driver is in the left-hand seat and looks around before moving. Controls are illustrative; learn the actual vehicle.

KörkortGo · M04-L02
M04-L02
Turn with a complete picture
Your goal: Plan observation, signalling, position and margins for turns and lane changes.
Requirements. Before a turn, check that it will not obstruct oncoming traffic or traffic on the
road you are entering. Pay attention to people travelling in the same direction, including those
behind you. Position early: normally the right-hand lane for a right turn and the left-hand lane
for a left turn where multiple approach lanes exist, subject to applicable signs, markings and
space provisions. On a two-way road, a left turn is normally prepared near the road centre; on a
one-way carriageway, near the left edge. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§24–29

Prohibitions, mandatory directions, one-way signs and lane arrows are separate sets. They are not all present at one
fictional junction.

KörkortGo · M10-L04
M10-L04
Make a realistic readiness plan
Your goal: Compare knowledge, practical performance and confidence, then plan further
learning and accessible examination preparation.
The official theory test covers vehicle knowledge/manoeuvring, environment, road safety, traffic
rules and personal factors. It checks understanding across those areas; memorising the wording
of practice questions is not equivalent preparation. The practical test requires you to apply
knowledge through vehicle checks, manoeuvres and driving in traffic. Trafikverket: category B
tests · Practical test
Current standard theory-test format, checked 1 October 2026: 70 questions, of which 65 count
towards the score; at least 52 points are needed to pass; standard time is 50 minutes. These
administrative figures can change, so verify them before booking. They are not a recommended
pass mark for this book's short learning checks. Trafikverket: theory-test format
Trafikverket provides language options, including English, and application routes for support
such as extended time, oral support or an interpreter where appropriate. Support generally
needs approval before the supported test can be booked. Check the current requirements and
apply early enough for a decision; do not assume that support can be added at the door.
Languages · Test support
Learning approach. Review three kinds of evidence: Can you explain the rule and its exceptions?
Can you recognise the situation without a prompt? Can you act safely and consistently during
supervised practice? A high confidence rating with little evidence is a learning signal, not a
readiness certificate.
Write your next practice plan in concrete terms: “Recognise cycle passages after a turn and
explain the duty before reaching them,” or “Demonstrate the safety check and explain each
defect response.” Revisit errors after a delay and in a changed scenario so that you are practising
understanding rather than recognising an answer.
Worked decision. A learner answers most checks correctly but still needs reminders to scan at
junctions. They continue targeted supervised practice instead of treating their theory score as
proof of practical readiness.

KörkortGo · M02-L01
M02-L01
Know what the controls tell you
Your goal: Explain the purpose of core controls, warning indicators, braking and steering
systems, and identify when further instructions are needed.
The practical test can include checking steering, brakes, tyres, lighting, fluids and warning
systems. You should be able to explain why you check them and propose action if you find a
problem. Before moving, adjust the seat, head restraint, steering wheel, mirrors and belt.
Trafikverket: safety check
Learning approach. While parked, locate the service brake, parking brake, transmission
controls, indicators, lighting controls, wipers, washers, demisting and hazard lights. Explain
what each control is for, then demonstrate it with your supervisor. “I can find it” and “I can use it
without losing attention” are different learning stages.
The service brake is used to reduce speed and stop; the parking brake helps secure a stationary
vehicle. Steering changes the vehicle's direction, but the tyres and road must provide the forces
needed to follow that direction. Braking and steering share the available friction: turning the
wheel is not proof that the car can follow the intended path. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§14
and 50 · VTI friction report, section 4.3
Vehicle-specific boundary. Control layouts, warning meanings and system checks differ. Use the
instructions for the actual vehicle before trying an unfamiliar function. This material does not
prescribe a universal brake-servo test, fluid-opening procedure or response to every dashboard
symbol. An unexplained warning is a reason to establish what is wrong before treating the car as
ready.

KörkortGo · M01-L03
M01-L03
Pressure is a driving risk
Your goal: Identify how peers, impulses, confidence and personal circumstances can
change a decision, and rehearse a refusal or alternative.
The official education syllabus asks learners to reflect on social influence, impulsive decisions,
personal motives and their own limitations. These are skills to practise, not labels to attach to an
age group or personality. Category B syllabus, chapter 5
Learning approach. Separate the journey's purpose from the feeling of the moment. “Get
everyone home” is a purpose. “Show that I can handle this bend quickly” is a different motive.
When a passenger's request changes your speed, following distance or willingness to overtake,
name the change before acting on it.
A useful personal boundary is a sentence you can use without debate: “I will stop somewhere
safe before changing the route”; “I am not passing here”; or “We need another way home.” These
are original rehearsal tools, not official scripts. Practise them before a difficult situation, and
agree that passengers will help with navigation only when asked.
Requirement. You still owe care to other road users and must adapt speed to conditions.
Cooperation does not authorise ignoring a traffic rule because another person is impatient.
Traffic Regulation, chapter 2 §1 and chapter 3 §14

KörkortGo · M05-L01
M05-L01
See the person behind the movement
Your goal: Anticipate the needs of different road users without assuming that everyone
sees, hears or moves as you do.
Requirements. Show particular consideration for children, older people, school patrols and
people whose disability or illness is apparent and affects their use of traffic. Reduce speed
appropriately near children, stopped passenger transport and other situations with foreseeable
risks. Give pedestrians sufficient room and time when meeting or passing them. Traffic
Regulation, chapter 2 §1 and chapter 3 §§15 and 58
Learning approach. Look for the space a person needs, not only the space they occupy now. A
child may be hidden by a parked car. A cyclist may need to move out from an obstruction. A
wheelchair user may need a usable kerb transition. You cannot reliably infer someone's hearing,
vision or intentions from a quick glance. Allow time and observe their movement rather than
demanding a response through the horn.
Observe people and possible movement
Children, cyclists and riders have different needs. Sensory-impairment panels are separate examples; absence of a
sign does not prove absence of risk.
A14 · Pedestrians ahead
Varning för gående
People often cross, walk on or remain near this stretch of road.
Allow for someone entering your path. Adult and child inside a
warning triangle.
Transportstyrelsen · official description

A passenger talks to the driver. In the road view, the car remains behind a van near a crest. Illustration, not a scale

M06-L04
Expect an interrupted route
Your goal: Interpret railway-crossing and roadworks information and approach changed
lanes, queues and barriers safely.
Railway requirements. Approach with particular care and at a speed that allows a stop before
the crossing. Do not enter when a train or tram is approaching, a red signal shows, an audible
warning sounds, a barrier is lowering, lowered or rising, or you might have to stop on the tracks.
Cross without unnecessary delay only when it is permitted and there is room beyond. Traffic
Regulation, chapter 2 §7
Railway warnings and crossing controls
Advance warnings, three/two/one countdown markers, crossbucks and active controls have different roles.
Countdown boards do not specify fixed metre intervals. A still image does not reproduce flashing or sound. No
crossing-ID number is invented.

KörkortGo · M01-L04
M01-L04
Plan the journey before the ignition
Your goal: Compare route, departure time, travel mode and passenger choices for safety,
accessibility and environmental impact.
Official advice · Trafikverket
Trafikverket recommends checking forecasts and traffic conditions, allowing time, taking breaks
on longer trips and preparing supplies appropriate to the season. The education syllabus also
asks you to consider whether a car is the right means of transport and how passengers or timing
affect a journey. Journey advice · Syllabus, chapters 4–5
Learning approach. Plan a usable journey rather than an ideal arrival time. Check where you can
rest, refuel or charge as appropriate to the vehicle, and stop legally at the destination. Arrange
restraints and space for passengers before departure. If the route has unfamiliar junctions or
restrictions, identify them while parked.
Compare realistic alternatives. Walking, cycling or public transport may suit some journeys; a car
may be necessary for others. Consider access needs, luggage, the return trip and the conditions
at the time you will actually travel. A plan that depends on rushing after a late appointment is
already fragile.

KörkortGo · M07-L04
M07-L04
Change the plan when risk grows
Your goal: Reassess a trip when weather, darkness, delays or passenger pressure
accumulate.
Learning approach. At a meaningful change—worsening visibility, an unexpected closure, a
missed rest opportunity—review the whole plan. Ask what has changed in the driver, vehicle,
route and time available. A manageable single difficulty may become demanding when several
occur together. This is a planning exercise, not a formula that assigns a numerical risk score.
Choose between continuing with a suitable margin, stopping safely, changing route, changing
driver if lawful and suitable, or cancelling the journey. The choice depends on the actual
conditions. A driver unable to maintain safe control must not continue merely because the
destination is close. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§1 and 14
The syllabus treats route choice, timing, passengers, fatigue and personal motives as parts of
driving competence. Use the same questions after a journey: Which warning did I notice early?
Which did I explain away because I wanted to finish? Syllabus, chapters 4–5

safe before changing the route”; “I am not passing here”; or “We need another way home.” These

agree that passengers will help with navigation only when asked.

M01-L02
Am I ready today?
Your goal: Decide whether to drive when tiredness, illness, medication, alcohol or drugs
may affect you, and explain a safer alternative.
Requirement. You must not drive when illness, exhaustion, alcohol, other substances or another
condition prevents safe control. A legal alcohol threshold is not a guarantee that you are capable
of driving safely. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1
Trafikverket states that the blood-alcohol limit for drink-driving is 0.2 per mille. For an
aggravated offence, factors include at least 1.0 per mille, substantial impairment, or driving that
creates a clear traffic danger. Non-prescribed narcotics are subject to a zero-tolerance rule.
Properly prescribed medication does not make impaired driving acceptable. Trafikverket:
drink-driving law · Alcohol, drugs and medication
Alcohol can affect judgement, attention, vision, reactions and coordination. Feeling normal does
not measure those effects. Performance can remain impaired the next day. Do not use a fixed
number of hours, a shower, coffee or a calculation as a personal clearance to drive. Ask your
prescriber or pharmacist about medicines and driving; do not change a prescribed treatment
simply to make a journey. Trafikverket: effects of alcohol and medicines
Learning approach. Before taking the keys, ask: Can I stay alert? Can I see and move well
enough? Has anything changed since I last drove? Can I concentrate on several developing
situations? If the answers are uncertain, make a different travel plan and resolve the uncertainty
first. Medical eligibility and day-to-day readiness are related but different: having a licence does
not mean you are fit for every journey. Medical requirements

Protect your attention

concentration cannot be maintained. Do not wait for a dramatic event to prove that you are too
tired. Trafikverket recommends setting out rested, allowing time and taking breaks on longer
journeys. No universal break interval in this material certifies that you can continue safely.

KörkortGo · M03-L04 · Continued
Continue the learning
Illustrative calculation, not a stopping-distance prediction. A speed of 50 km/h is
approximately 13.9 metres per second: 50 ÷ 3.6. If a hypothetical response delay is one second,
that is about 14 metres before braking begins. At 80 km/h the same assumed delay consumes
about 22 metres. These figures are unit conversions using an assumed delay; people do not all
react in one second, and braking distance has not yet been added.
Learning approach. Scan far enough ahead to see developing situations, while revisiting the
near area, mirrors and places where someone may enter. Avoid staring at one hazard until
everything else disappears from attention. Increase your margin when information is poor. A
timed following-gap check can help you notice a short gap, but no fixed number is safe in every
condition.

KörkortGo · M03-L04 · Continued
Continue the learning
Illustrative calculation, not a stopping-distance prediction. A speed of 50 km/h is
approximately 13.9 metres per second: 50 ÷ 3.6. If a hypothetical response delay is one second,
that is about 14 metres before braking begins. At 80 km/h the same assumed delay consumes
about 22 metres. These figures are unit conversions using an assumed delay; people do not all
react in one second, and braking distance has not yet been added.
Learning approach. Scan far enough ahead to see developing situations, while revisiting the
near area, mirrors and places where someone may enter. Avoid staring at one hazard until
everything else disappears from attention. Increase your margin when information is poor. A
timed following-gap check can help you notice a short gap, but no fixed number is safe in every
condition.

KörkortGo · M07-L03
M07-L03
Protect your attention
Your goal: Recognise distraction, stress and fatigue and choose an interruption or
alternative travel plan.
Requirements. During road travel, a driver may use communication equipment only if it does
not adversely affect driving. Holding the equipment in the hand while using it is prohibited.
Hands-free use is therefore not automatically acceptable: the effect on driving still matters. You
must also not drive when exhaustion or another condition prevents safe control.
Transportstyrelsen: communication equipment · Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1 and chapter 4
§10e
Learning approach. Prepare navigation before setting off, place the phone away from casual
handling and agree when passengers can help. If a conversation, screen task or emotional
reaction is consuming the attention needed for the road, end it. A safe place to stop is the place
to resolve a complicated route or urgent message.
Treat fatigue as a reason to change the journey. Plan rest opportunities and stop safely when
concentration cannot be maintained. Do not wait for a dramatic event to prove that you are too
tired. Trafikverket recommends setting out rested, allowing time and taking breaks on longer
journeys. No universal break interval in this material certifies that you can continue safely.

Your goal: Plan anticipatory driving that reduces unnecessary energy use while preserving

route and timing decisions. Avoid claiming a fixed percentage saving: load, road, weather,

M09-L01
Look beyond the exhaust
Your goal: Compare climate, air-quality and noise effects without assuming that a vehicle
has no environmental impact.
Transportstyrelsen distinguishes several effects. Greenhouse-gas emissions relate to the amount
of travel, fuels, energy efficiency and electrification. Air pollution includes exhaust emissions and
wear particles from brakes, tyres and the road. Noise is another effect, with tyre-road noise
becoming important as speed rises. These are different measures: improving one does not prove
that every environmental effect has disappeared. Climate and energy · Air quality · Noise
Learning approach. Ask what a comparison includes. Does an emissions figure describe a test
result, the actual journey or a broader lifecycle? Are you comparing equal distances and
occupancy? If the basis is missing, avoid a confident numerical conclusion. This lesson does not
assign a universal emissions saving to a powertrain or declare a whole journey “zero impact.”
A plug-in hybrid combines electrical and combustion-engine operation. Transportstyrelsen
changed the weighting used for new registrations in 2026 to better reflect the mix of those
modes. The general lesson is to understand what a reported figure represents; it is not a promise
about your next journey's consumption. Transportstyrelsen: plug-in-hybrid weighting
Worked decision. Two vehicles are advertised using different environmental measures. One
figure describes exhaust emissions under a test procedure; another describes noise. The learner
does not rank them as though both figures measure the same thing. They first identify the
question being answered and the information still missing.

Look ahead and preserve room
The teal car approaches a queue on the right side of the road. Look ahead, retain room to stop and keep the crossing

accelerate simply to close the gap, and you do not roll into a crossing to preserve momentum.

KörkortGo · M08-L04
M08-L04
Know what assistance cannot do
Your goal: Explain why safety systems and powertrain differences do not remove your
duties to observe and control.
Trafikverket describes modern protection as including crashworthiness and systems such as
lane assistance and automatic emergency braking. These functions can help, but a good safety
rating is not a promise that any collision can be avoided. Recent official crash testing also shows
the limits of automatic braking in severe truck-trailer collision scenarios. Crash safety ·
Trafikverket: braking and truck-trailer tests
ABS is anti-lock braking. It helps retain the ability to develop steering and braking forces
together, within available friction. Stability control reduces the risk of skid crashes; it does not
create extra road grip or excuse excessive speed. The driver still has to maintain control and an
appropriate speed. VTI friction report, section 4.3 · Trafikverket: tyre and stability advice · Traffic
Regulation, chapter 3 §14
Powertrain awareness. A plug-in hybrid can operate on electricity and with a combustion
engine. That difference matters when interpreting fuel use and emissions: do not assume that
every journey is electrically powered. Transportstyrelsen: plug-in hybrids
For the actual vehicle, establish how it becomes ready to move, how drive and reverse are
selected, how it is secured, and what warnings or assistance limitations need attention. Do not
transfer a universal gear-change, engine-speed, coasting or brake-check recipe between
manual, automatic, hybrid and electric vehicles. Vehicle-specific procedures need the vehicle's
own instructions and practical teaching. The curriculum's role is to help you identify those
questions, not guess their answers.

KörkortGo · M09-L03
M09-L03
Choose the journey as well as the car
Your goal: Compare combining trips, walking, cycling, public transport and driving for a
realistic personal journey.
The syllabus includes transport choices and the way personal circumstances influence them. A
useful comparison recognises that people's access needs, schedules and available services
differ. Category B syllabus, chapters 4–5
Learning approach. Start with the purpose: reaching work, collecting goods, accompanying a
person or making a visit. Then list workable options. Could two errands be combined? Could a
nearby trip be walked or cycled safely? Is public transport available for both directions? If you
share a car journey, can everyone use the required protection and travel without creating a
rushed schedule?
Do not replace one unrealistic assumption with another. A route may be short but inaccessible to
a particular person. A service may run outward but not at the return time. A car may solve those
needs, while a different choice suits the following day's journey. The exercise is to make the
choice deliberately.

Check where the vehicle can go
Your goal: Find official environmental-zone information and determine what to verify
before entering.
Requirements. Municipalities can introduce environmental zones under the national
framework. Class 1 concerns heavy buses and heavy goods vehicles; class 2 concerns passenger

M03-L04
Leave room to respond
Your goal: Explain how observation, speed, reaction, braking, grip and following space
affect your options.
Requirements. Choose a speed that preserves control and lets you stop within the road you can
see and before a foreseeable obstruction. Your distance from the vehicle ahead must allow for it
slowing or stopping. Weather, visibility, road condition, vehicle condition and loading all matter.
Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§2 and 14–16
For an ordinary car, the general speed limits are 50 km/h within a built-up area and 70 km/h
outside it, unless another applicable limit has been prescribed. The motorway default is 110
km/h; 120 km/h can be prescribed. Local and road-specific limits often differ, and a lower
vehicle-combination limit still applies. Read the current signs and conditions rather than
selecting a speed from the road’s appearance. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §17, chapter 4 §20
and chapter 9 §1
Limits and road regimes
Numeric maximum-speed examples are independent. Start and end types are labelled individually; unequal values
do not form a sequence.
C31 · Maximum speed
Hastighetsbegränsning
Do not exceed the displayed speed in km/h. A junction alone
does not necessarily end the limit, and conditions may require
a lower speed. Red-bordered yellow circle displaying 30:
maximum 30 km/h.
Transportstyrelsen · official description

KörkortGo · M03-L04 · Continued
Continue the learning
Illustrative calculation, not a stopping-distance prediction. A speed of 50 km/h is
approximately 13.9 metres per second: 50 ÷ 3.6. If a hypothetical response delay is one second,
that is about 14 metres before braking begins. At 80 km/h the same assumed delay consumes
about 22 metres. These figures are unit conversions using an assumed delay; people do not all
react in one second, and braking distance has not yet been added.
Learning approach. Scan far enough ahead to see developing situations, while revisiting the
near area, mirrors and places where someone may enter. Avoid staring at one hazard until
everything else disappears from attention. Increase your margin when information is poor. A
timed following-gap check can help you notice a short gap, but no fixed number is safe in every
condition.

KörkortGo · M10-L04
M10-L04
Make a realistic readiness plan
Your goal: Compare knowledge, practical performance and confidence, then plan further
learning and accessible examination preparation.
The official theory test covers vehicle knowledge/manoeuvring, environment, road safety, traffic
rules and personal factors. It checks understanding across those areas; memorising the wording
of practice questions is not equivalent preparation. The practical test requires you to apply
knowledge through vehicle checks, manoeuvres and driving in traffic. Trafikverket: category B
tests · Practical test
Current standard theory-test format, checked 1 October 2026: 70 questions, of which 65 count
towards the score; at least 52 points are needed to pass; standard time is 50 minutes. These
administrative figures can change, so verify them before booking. They are not a recommended
pass mark for this book's short learning checks. Trafikverket: theory-test format
Trafikverket provides language options, including English, and application routes for support
such as extended time, oral support or an interpreter where appropriate. Support generally
needs approval before the supported test can be booked. Check the current requirements and
apply early enough for a decision; do not assume that support can be added at the door.
Languages · Test support
Learning approach. Review three kinds of evidence: Can you explain the rule and its exceptions?
Can you recognise the situation without a prompt? Can you act safely and consistently during
supervised practice? A high confidence rating with little evidence is a learning signal, not a
readiness certificate.
Write your next practice plan in concrete terms: “Recognise cycle passages after a turn and
explain the duty before reaching them,” or “Demonstrate the safety check and explain each
defect response.” Revisit errors after a delay and in a changed scenario so that you are practising
understanding rather than recognising an answer.
Worked decision. A learner answers most checks correctly but still needs reminders to scan at
junctions. They continue targeted supervised practice instead of treating their theory score as
proof of practical readiness.

Read the rural road
Your goal: Identify risks from bends, crests, narrow roads, animals and slow vehicles and
justify speed and position changes.
Requirements. Keep right when meeting another vehicle and leave a safe lateral gap. If an
obstruction on your side prevents a safe meeting, stop if necessary to let the approaching
vehicle pass. Your speed must suit the visible road and foreseeable hazards, with particular care
at bends, crests and narrow meetings. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§14–15 and 30

portion hidden behind a crest and the next place someone might join. Never extend the clear
section in your imagination. A vehicle emerging from a field or a cyclist beyond a bend changes
what seemed to be an empty road.

Your goal: Anticipate the needs of different road users without assuming that everyone
sees, hears or moves as you do.

risks. Give pedestrians sufficient room and time when meeting or passing them. Traffic

vision or intentions from a quick glance. Allow time and observe their movement rather than
demanding a response through the horn.

KörkortGo · M06-L02
M06-L02
Is passing worth the risk?
Your goal: Compare waiting with overtaking using visibility, speed difference, space and a
safe completion path.
Requirements. Overtake only without danger and with sufficient clear road. Do not start when a
following driver has begun overtaking, or pass on the left when the vehicle ahead signals an
intended leftward movement. Leave safe lateral clearance and a safe return opportunity. When
being overtaken, do not increase speed or otherwise make the pass harder. Traffic Regulation,
chapter 3 §§31–38
The normal passing side is left. Exceptions include a vehicle turning or clearly preparing to turn
left, and the specified rules for marked same-direction lanes on roads limited to 70 km/h or less.
Passing in queues or destination lanes has separate provisions; it does not remove the need to
protect people at crossings. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§7, 31 and 41–42
Restrictions to recognise. Overtaking is generally prohibited immediately before or in a road
junction, with specified exceptions for right-side overtaking, police/signal control, or an
established yielding/stopping duty on the crossing road. Similar restrictions apply at level
crossings, with exceptions for barriers or road-junction-type traffic signals. At an obscured bend
or crest, do not use an opposing lane to overtake; the detailed provision contains limited
exceptions. Section 39 also contains an exception for passing two-wheeled vehicles without
sidecars. That exception does not override the danger prohibition, continuous-line restrictions
or the uncontrolled-crossing prohibition. None of these exceptions proves a manoeuvre safe.
Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §39
Do not overtake immediately before or on an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing, uncontrolled
cycle passage or cycle crossing. Where parallel-lane passing is legally not classified as
overtaking, the special crossing rule still requires a speed allowing an immediate stop for a
person on the crossing or passage. Obey signs and continuous-line restrictions as well. Traffic
Regulation, chapter 3 §§11, 40–41

KörkortGo · M06-L02 · Illustration
Assess the whole passing path
Learning approach. Before moving, identify the full pass and return path, not merely the first
gap. If completing it depends on another driver braking or on exceeding the limit, decline it.
Small apparent time savings are not a reason to consume every margin. Trafikverket: speed and
journey time
Following a slower vehicle towards a hidden bend. The visible straight does not establish a complete pass and
return path. The depicted spacing is illustrative, not a recommended following distance.
Worked decision. A vehicle ahead travels slightly slower than you want. An approaching bend
hides the final part of the pass. You stay behind at a useful distance. The first few clear metres do
not establish a complete overtaking opportunity.

KörkortGo · M07-L02
M07-L02
Grip is a changing resource
Your goal: Explain how surface conditions, tyres and driver inputs affect stability, steering
and braking.
Tyres need friction to change the vehicle's speed and direction. Braking while cornering shares
that capacity; ABS can help preserve steering forces during braking, but the available friction still
limits the result. Water, snow and ice change the conditions at the tyre contact, so dry-road
expectations cannot simply be carried into them. VTI friction report, sections 4.2–4.3
Warnings about grip
Independent slippery-road and loose-chippings warnings. Observe the actual surface; these warnings are not
limited to winter.
A10 · Slippery road
Varning för slirig väg
The road may be slippery. Do not assume that the warning
refers only to snow or ice. Skidding car inside a red-bordered
yellow triangle.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
A11 · Loose chippings
Varning för stenskott
There is a risk of stones being thrown up. This warning is not
normally used where that risk is routine, such as a gravel road.
Car wheel throws stones inside a warning triangle.
Transportstyrelsen · official description

KörkortGo · M07-L02 · Illustration
Prepare before grip changes
Learning approach. Reduce speed and increase space before reaching uncertain grip. Avoid
demanding abrupt braking, steering and acceleration together. Do not experiment with skid
recovery in ordinary traffic. Establish the actual vehicle's emergency-braking behaviour through
appropriate instruction and risk training. Trafikverket: winter driving advice · Risk training
A dry-looking foreground leads towards a shaded winter bend. The surface appearance is a reason to reassess, not a
measurement of friction. No skid-recovery technique or guaranteed tyre performance is shown.
Worked decision. Your car has suitable winter tyres, but the next bend is partly shaded and looks
different from the road behind. You reduce speed before the bend and preserve margin.
Equipment does not establish the grip at that particular point.

KörkortGo · M03-L04
M03-L04
Leave room to respond
Your goal: Explain how observation, speed, reaction, braking, grip and following space
affect your options.
Requirements. Choose a speed that preserves control and lets you stop within the road you can
see and before a foreseeable obstruction. Your distance from the vehicle ahead must allow for it
slowing or stopping. Weather, visibility, road condition, vehicle condition and loading all matter.
Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§2 and 14–16
For an ordinary car, the general speed limits are 50 km/h within a built-up area and 70 km/h
outside it, unless another applicable limit has been prescribed. The motorway default is 110
km/h; 120 km/h can be prescribed. Local and road-specific limits often differ, and a lower
vehicle-combination limit still applies. Read the current signs and conditions rather than
selecting a speed from the road’s appearance. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §17, chapter 4 §20
and chapter 9 §1
Limits and road regimes
Numeric maximum-speed examples are independent. Start and end types are labelled individually; unequal values
do not form a sequence.
C31 · Maximum speed
Hastighetsbegränsning
Do not exceed the displayed speed in km/h. A junction alone
does not necessarily end the limit, and conditions may require
a lower speed. Red-bordered yellow circle displaying 30:
maximum 30 km/h.
Transportstyrelsen · official description

KörkortGo · M07-L01
M07-L01
Drive within what you can see
Your goal: Choose a visibility and lighting strategy for darkness, fog and glare.
Requirements. Your speed must allow a stop within the visible road and before foreseeable
hazards. Darkness does not create a separate allowance to travel beyond the distance you can
assess. Keep the required lamps on; daytime running lights alone may be insufficient when
conditions deteriorate. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§14–15 and 68–71
Another changing condition: crosswinds
Independent crosswind warnings. The windsock shows the wind direction; neither example is a fog warning or a
headlight instruction.
A24 · Crosswinds
Varning för sidvind
Strong crosswinds commonly occur on this stretch. The
symbol is adapted to local conditions. Windsock extends
towards the left.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
A24-2 · Crosswinds
Varning för sidvind
Strong crosswinds commonly occur on this stretch. The
symbol is adapted to local conditions. Windsock extends
towards the right.
Transportstyrelsen · official description

KörkortGo · M07-L01 · Continued
Continue the learning
Use main beam when needed for a sufficient field of view, but not where the road is adequately
lit, where it can dazzle an approaching driver or an adjacent rail/ship operator, or at close
distance behind another vehicle. Dipped beam is the usual driving light. In fog or heavy
precipitation, front fog lights may replace dipped beam; the prohibited combinations must not
be used together. A rear fog light is restricted to fog, heavy precipitation or comparable reduced
visibility and must not dazzle a following driver. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§69–72
Learning approach. Make lighting and speed one decision. If you dip the lights and can see less
far, reassess speed immediately. Check the edges of the visible road for people and animals
rather than assuming a dark area is empty. Keep windows and mirrors clear enough for a useful
view and learn demisting controls before a difficult journey.
Automatic lighting is an aid, not confirmation that every required lamp is on. In a car whose
daytime-light mode leaves the rear lights off, check the actual setting when darkness or bad
weather arrives. Transportstyrelsen: vehicle lighting

KörkortGo · M05-L01
M05-L01
See the person behind the movement
Your goal: Anticipate the needs of different road users without assuming that everyone
sees, hears or moves as you do.
Requirements. Show particular consideration for children, older people, school patrols and
people whose disability or illness is apparent and affects their use of traffic. Reduce speed
appropriately near children, stopped passenger transport and other situations with foreseeable
risks. Give pedestrians sufficient room and time when meeting or passing them. Traffic
Regulation, chapter 2 §1 and chapter 3 §§15 and 58
Learning approach. Look for the space a person needs, not only the space they occupy now. A
child may be hidden by a parked car. A cyclist may need to move out from an obstruction. A
wheelchair user may need a usable kerb transition. You cannot reliably infer someone's hearing,
vision or intentions from a quick glance. Allow time and observe their movement rather than
demanding a response through the horn.

M10-L02
When someone may be hurt
Your goal: Identify scene-safety, emergency-contact and first-aid learning needs following
a collision.
Requirements. If involved in a traffic accident, remain at the scene, help injured people to the
extent of your ability and assist with necessary measures. Provide your name, address and
information when requested by another involved person or someone whose property was
damaged. Notify the owner or police promptly if damaged property has nobody present to
receive the information. Notify police promptly for a personal injury that is not insignificant.
Traffic Regulation, chapter 2 §8
A vehicle creating danger or obstruction after a collision should be moved to a suitable place.
However, where someone has died or been seriously injured, move it only if it endangers other
traffic, and preserve evidence as required. Staying at the scene does not mean standing in an
active traffic lane. Protect yourself and others while arranging help. Traffic Regulation, chapter 2
§8
Emergency response. At danger to life, call 112. Give the location, direction of travel, what
happened and what dangers you can see; follow the operator's instructions. Make observations
from a safe position rather than walking into moving traffic to gather details. Trafikverket:
emergency contact

direction of travel, what happened and immediate dangers. Follow the operator's instructions.

call 112 and describe the immediate traffic danger from a protected position, following
instructions and helping within your ability. Photographing damage is not the first priority.

Transportstyrelsen · official description
First-aid reference. Use 1177's first-aid guidance to learn more about helping someone in an
acute situation, including when a person is unconscious or has breathing difficulties. Practical
first-aid training can help you prepare. This lesson is deliberately brief and does not reproduce
clinical procedures or a pulse-check sequence. In an emergency, call 112 rather than spending
time searching a website.
Wildlife collisions. Trafikverket advises calling 112 and marking the collision location safely so
responders can find it, even if the animal has left. Avoid approaching an injured animal. Its
guidance gives a separate precaution for wild boar, bear, lynx and wolf: continue 200 m before
stopping and marking, then call police immediately. Only move the vehicle when safe and
possible; explain the actual collision location and the animal's direction clearly. This is agency
safety guidance, not a claim that every animal species has identical statutory reporting rules.

evidence.page_text:
KörkortGo · M10-L01
M10-L01
When the car cannot continue
Your goal: Compare a breakdown on an ordinary road, a motorway and in a tunnel.
Requirement. If a breakdown leaves a vehicle where stopping is prohibited, it must be moved to
a suitable place as soon as possible, subject to the special rules for an accident scene. Warning
obligations depend on the situation. A warning triangle must give approaching drivers enough
warning; the law does not prescribe one universal distance for every road. Traffic Regulation,
chapter 3 §§51 and 57
Official motorway/2+1-road advice. If possible, reach the safest available stopping place.
Switch on hazard lights, warn other traffic and leave the vehicle and carriageway promptly. Move
away from traffic, outside a barrier where one exists. Trafikverket recommends placing the
triangle at least 100 m away, preferably farther, and taking care while doing so, walking at the
side and outside the barrier where possible. Do not expose yourself in the traffic lane to carry out
a roadside repair. Call professional recovery; call 112 when life is in danger. Trafikverket:
breakdown advice
Tunnel advice is different. Use hazard lights, move towards the edge or an emergency bay if
possible and switch off the engine. For a non-urgent incident, Trafikverket advises staying in the
car or protected from traffic close to it while calling for assistance. In an urgent situation, leave
for the nearest emergency exit and use the assistance point, emergency phone or 112. In a fire,
leave and reach an emergency exit; follow signs, announcements and emergency personnel. Do
not turn a non-urgent-tunnel recommendation into advice to stay beside a fire. Trafikverket:
tunnels

evidence.page_text:
KörkortGo · M02-L03
M02-L03
Protect everyone inside
Your goal: Select suitable restraints for passengers and explain how belts, headrests and
airbags work together.
Requirements. In an ordinary car journey, occupants must use an available belt-equipped place
and wear the belt. Children under 135 cm normally need an appropriate child restraint. The
driver must take appropriate measures to ensure passengers under 15 use the required
protection. Limited exceptions exist, including specified short occasional journeys, and should
not become a routine travel plan. Seat-belt rules · Traffic Regulation, chapter 4 §§10–10d
For a child aged three or more but shorter than 135 cm, an occasional short transport without an
available child restraint is an exception only under the stated conditions: use the belt where
possible and not the front seat of a passenger car or light goods vehicle. For a child under three,
the exception is an occasional short taxi trip, also excluding the front seat. Plan with the correct
restraint instead. Transportstyrelsen: child rules
Official recommendations. Trafikverket recommends rear-facing travel until at least four to five
years, preferably longer. Transportstyrelsen's advice says as long as possible, normally around
four. These are recommendations, not a single legal birthday on which to turn the seat. Choose
equipment that fits the child and car and stays within its approved size and weight limits.
Reaching 135 cm does not automatically produce good adult-belt fit. Trafikverket: children in
cars · Transportstyrelsen: child protection
Never place a rear-facing child restraint in front of an active passenger airbag. Trafikverket
advises at least 140 cm in front of an active airbag unless the manufacturer recommends
otherwise; Transportstyrelsen gives more conservative advice for children in restraints. Resolve
seating and airbag compatibility using the vehicle and restraint instructions before travelling. An
airbag supplements a belt; it does not replace one. Adjust the head restraint for the person
occupying the seat. Children in cars · Airbags · Seats and head restraints

Apply the learning
An adult and child stand beside an open rear door. The empty booster and rear bench face forwards. This scene
does not demonstrate installation or belt fit; follow the child-restraint and vehicle instructions.

KörkortGo · M03-L04 · Continued
Continue the learning
Illustrative calculation, not a stopping-distance prediction. A speed of 50 km/h is
approximately 13.9 metres per second: 50 ÷ 3.6. If a hypothetical response delay is one second,
that is about 14 metres before braking begins. At 80 km/h the same assumed delay consumes
about 22 metres. These figures are unit conversions using an assumed delay; people do not all
react in one second, and braking distance has not yet been added.
Learning approach. Scan far enough ahead to see developing situations, while revisiting the
near area, mirrors and places where someone may enter. Avoid staring at one hazard until
everything else disappears from attention. Increase your margin when information is poor. A
timed following-gap check can help you notice a short gap, but no fixed number is safe in every
condition.

KörkortGo · M07-L02
M07-L02
Grip is a changing resource
Your goal: Explain how surface conditions, tyres and driver inputs affect stability, steering
and braking.
Tyres need friction to change the vehicle's speed and direction. Braking while cornering shares
that capacity; ABS can help preserve steering forces during braking, but the available friction still
limits the result. Water, snow and ice change the conditions at the tyre contact, so dry-road
expectations cannot simply be carried into them. VTI friction report, sections 4.2–4.3
Warnings about grip
Independent slippery-road and loose-chippings warnings. Observe the actual surface; these warnings are not
limited to winter.
A10 · Slippery road
Varning för slirig väg

refers only to snow or ice. Skidding car inside a red-bordered
yellow triangle.

A11 · Loose chippings

normally used where that risk is routine, such as a gravel road.

evidence.page_text:
KörkortGo · M07-L02 · Continued
Continue the learning
Requirements for ordinary light cars and their trailers, checked 1 October 2026. Between 1
December and 31 March, winter tyres or equivalent equipment are required when winter
conditions exist. Snow, ice, slush or frost on any part of the road counts; police determine
conditions at the location. The minimum tread depth for the ordinary light-vehicle case is 3 mm.
Studless winter tyres for the car need the mountain/snowflake marking. Winter tyres
Studded tyres are permitted from 1 October to 15 April and outside that period when winter
conditions exist or are expected. Do not mix studded and non-studded tyres on an ordinary
passenger car or light goods vehicle. In winter conditions, a studded towing car requires a
studded trailer; the reverse combination is allowed. A light-trailer transition permits specified
winter-designed M+S tyres through 30 November 2028. Exemptions and heavier-vehicle cases
need their own checks; they are not the ordinary car rule. Winter tyres · Traffic Regulation,
chapter 4 §§18a–18d
Check local studded-tyre restrictions
Seasonal permission to use studs does not override a local prohibition. This road sign is not a tyre sidewall marking.
C44 · No studded-tyre motor vehicles except class II mopeds
Förbud mot trafik med annat motordrivet fordon med dubbdäck
än moped klass II
The prohibition concerns motor vehicles with studded tyres.
Class II mopeds are included only if a supplementary panel
says so. Studded tyre crossed by a red diagonal.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
For summer conditions, the minimum tread depth is 1.6 mm. Transportstyrelsen recommends
placing the tyres with the best grip or greatest tread depth at the rear and checking pressure
against the vehicle's instructions. A legal minimum is not a promise of equal performance in
every condition. Transportstyrelsen: tyres

accelerating towards it and then braking sharply. Choose a suitable speed and preserve a gap
that lets you adapt smoothly. This is not an instruction to delay necessary braking: safe control

route and timing decisions. Avoid claiming a fixed percentage saving: load, road, weather,

Your goal: Use entitlement and vehicle information to assess a car or trailer combination.
Requirements. Ordinary category B permits a passenger car or light goods vehicle with a total
weight of no more than 3,500 kg. For trailers, either the trailer's total weight is at most 750 kg, or,
if above 750 kg, the car and trailer's combined total weights must not exceed 3,500 kg. The first
route can therefore permit a combination up to 4,250 kg; it does not mean every 4,250 kg
combination is permitted on ordinary B. Category B · Car with trailer
Extended B (B96) permits combined total weights up to 4,250 kg, without increasing the car's
3,500 kg limit. Under the ordinary current BE rule, the towing car is still limited to 3,500 kg total
weight and the trailer or trailers may have combined total weights up to 3,500 kg. Older
entitlements and conditions can differ; check the individual licence rather than applying a
current-new-licence example to everyone. This book is not a full B96 or BE course. Trailer
entitlement guide
Two tests. Entitlement uses registered total weights. Technical towing limits also restrict what
the particular car may pull in its actual loaded state. Emptying a trailer may reduce its actual
weight without changing its registered total weight, so it may solve a technical-weight problem
but not an entitlement problem. Towing weights

A check before moving
Your goal: Organise a safety check of tyres, lights, visibility and vehicle condition, and
distinguish a defect from a reason to seek help.
Learning approach. Work around the car, then through the driving position. Look for damaged
tyres, an unusual stance, leaks or obstructions; confirm that windows and mirrors permit a
useful view. Check required lights and indicators, and ask for help where a second person is
useful. Check washers and wipers before you need them in poor weather. Use the actual
vehicle's instructions for fluid levels and service checks. These groups reflect the official
practical-test safety check; they are not a guarantee that a quick walkaround detects every
defect. Trafikverket: safety check
Requirements. Tyres must be suitable for the vehicle, including load capacity and applicable
speed capability. The registration information and approved vehicle requirements matter when
changing tyre sizes. Do not assume any wheel that physically fits is suitable. Transportstyrelsen:
tyre requirements
Required lighting must work and be used appropriately. Some cars can run daytime lights
without rear lights; the driver must ensure suitable front, rear and side lighting is on in darkness,
twilight or poor weather. A trailer's lighting must be on during travel. Automatic settings may
need manual intervention. Transportstyrelsen: vehicle lighting

KörkortGo · M07-L01 · Continued
Continue the learning
Use main beam when needed for a sufficient field of view, but not where the road is adequately
lit, where it can dazzle an approaching driver or an adjacent rail/ship operator, or at close
distance behind another vehicle. Dipped beam is the usual driving light. In fog or heavy
precipitation, front fog lights may replace dipped beam; the prohibited combinations must not
be used together. A rear fog light is restricted to fog, heavy precipitation or comparable reduced
visibility and must not dazzle a following driver. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§69–72
Learning approach. Make lighting and speed one decision. If you dip the lights and can see less
far, reassess speed immediately. Check the edges of the visible road for people and animals
rather than assuming a dark area is empty. Keep windows and mirrors clear enough for a useful
view and learn demisting controls before a difficult journey.
Automatic lighting is an aid, not confirmation that every required lamp is on. In a car whose
daytime-light mode leaves the rear lights off, check the actual setting when darkness or bad
weather arrives. Transportstyrelsen: vehicle lighting

Reassess the visible road
Rain and darkness shorten the usable view. The teal car travels on the right. Reassess speed and check the actual
exterior-light setting; the illustration does not identify a lamp mode or a measured stopping distance.
Worked decision. Rain becomes heavy during a daytime trip. The dashboard remains
illuminated, but the driver checks and selects the appropriate exterior lighting rather than
inferring that the rear lights must be on. The driver also reduces speed for the shorter usable

Your goal: Explain the purpose of core controls, warning indicators, braking and steering
systems, and identify when further instructions are needed.

systems. You should be able to explain why you check them and propose action if you find a
problem. Before moving, adjust the seat, head restraint, steering wheel, mirrors and belt.

controls, indicators, lighting controls, wipers, washers, demisting and hazard lights. Explain
what each control is for, then demonstrate it with your supervisor. “I can find it” and “I can use it

needed to follow that direction. Braking and steering share the available friction: turning the
wheel is not proof that the car can follow the intended path. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§14
and 50 · VTI friction report, section 4.3

instructions for the actual vehicle before trying an unfamiliar function. This material does not
prescribe a universal brake-servo test, fluid-opening procedure or response to every dashboard
symbol. An unexplained warning is a reason to establish what is wrong before treating the car as
ready.

M08-L03
Keep the car legally ready
Your goal: Build an ownership checklist for registration, insurance, inspection and vehicle
status.
Requirements. The registered owner of an on-road car must have compulsory motor insurance.
Not using the car, or having a defect or driving prohibition, does not by itself end that obligation;
formal off-road status matters. Compulsory insurance covers specified traffic injuries and
damage to others, not every loss to your own car. Optional cover varies by policy. Compulsory
motor insurance
For an ordinary car or light goods vehicle up to 3,500 kg, the normal inspection sequence is: first
by 36 months after the month of first use, second by 24 months after the first inspection month,
then by 14 months after the preceding inspection month. Check the recorded date and any
special category or exemption for your vehicle. An earlier inspection changes the next
calculation; an old reminder is not proof of the current deadline. Inspection intervals
An on-road registration status, valid insurance and completed inspection answer different
questions. Check the vehicle's status and any prohibition before use, and deal with tax
obligations through the current official service. A car being physically driveable does not
establish legal readiness. On-road and off-road status
Ownership process. Transportstyrelsen currently provides eligible private-person transfers
through Mina sidor; other cases may require the latest registration certificate part 2. The service
has eligibility conditions. Consult the current instructions instead of relying on an old app or a
remembered screen sequence. Part 1 and the vehicle enquiry service provide technical
information; protect ownership documents appropriately. Ownership transfer · Registration
certificate
Worked decision. A buyer collects an on-road car but assumes the seller's insurance is enough
for the trip home. The buyer checks the transfer and arranges the required cover from the
applicable ownership date before driving. The sale does not transfer the seller's insurance as
personal cover for the buyer.

evidence.page_text:
KörkortGo · M03-L04 · Continued
Continue the learning
Illustrative calculation, not a stopping-distance prediction. A speed of 50 km/h is
approximately 13.9 metres per second: 50 ÷ 3.6. If a hypothetical response delay is one second,
that is about 14 metres before braking begins. At 80 km/h the same assumed delay consumes
about 22 metres. These figures are unit conversions using an assumed delay; people do not all
react in one second, and braking distance has not yet been added.
Learning approach. Scan far enough ahead to see developing situations, while revisiting the
near area, mirrors and places where someone may enter. Avoid staring at one hazard until
everything else disappears from attention. Increase your margin when information is poor. A
timed following-gap check can help you notice a short gap, but no fixed number is safe in every
condition.

Illustrative calculation, not a stopping-distance prediction. A speed of 50 km/h is
approximately 13.9 metres per second: 50 ÷ 3.6. If a hypothetical response delay is one second,
that is about 14 metres before braking begins. At 80 km/h the same assumed delay consumes
about 22 metres. These figures are unit conversions using an assumed delay; people do not all
react in one second, and braking distance has not yet been added.
Learning approach. Scan far enough ahead to see developing situations, while revisiting the
near area, mirrors and places where someone may enter. Avoid staring at one hazard until
everything else disappears from attention. Increase your margin when information is poor. A
timed following-gap check can help you notice a short gap, but no fixed number is safe in every
condition.

questions.rationale: Page 246 defines maximum load as total weight minus defined ready weight. Use the figures supplied and do not count the driver twice.

Make the load part of the safety
check
Your goal: Distinguish weight terms and assess securing, capacity and trailer suitability.
Term
Meaning for this lesson
Tjänstevikt
Vehicle in its defined ready-for-use state; a car's figure includes the driver, while a
trailer's does not include cargo.
Totalvikt
Registered maximum weight, built from the defined unladen/ready weight and
maximum load.
Bruttovikt
Actual weight transmitted to the road at that time.
Maximilast
Total weight minus the defined ready weight: the maximum passenger/cargo
load.
Use the official definitions when reading registration data. Do not count the driver twice in an
exercise that starts from a car's defined tjänstevikt, and do not assume a paper figure measures
the load you have actually added. Weight definitions
